`duty.py` takes the tariff schedule's location from a `DUTYBOOK` environment variable, which the README doesn't mention. If that variable isn't set, the script stops with an error. I pointed it at the only schedule in the repo, so I ran it as `DUTYBOOK=schedules/hs-2026.csv python3 duty.py manifests/ship-0412.csv`. I didn't change `duty.py`. I also saved a note to memory so the next session sets the variable from the start.
